messages.author: 2c505cfee89b0f86
messages.subject: Multiple linked QTLs
parts:
Hello all,

I am working with several crosses that have multiple, fairly closely
linked QTLs. However, I'm not sure if that completely explains what is
occurring. What seems to happen is I run scanone, and it will identify
the QTL of highest LOD. Then if I run makeqtl and fitqtl it will be
highly significant. But, if I then search for additional qtls using
addqtl it will identify another QTL around 1 to 4 cM away. If this is
added to the model they will be significant under fitqtl but less so
than before. This will happen over and over again until there are
around 4-5 linked QTLs in the model. This seems to be an artifact,
but what is the best way to handle something like this? Below is an
example of output from fitqtl with significant QTLs on chromosome 3 at
35 and 36 cM, then addqtl identifies on at 34 cM. The LODs are
progressively smaller, but significant.

Full model result
----------------------------------
Model formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 + Q4

df SS MS LOD %var Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue(F)
Model 8 980.6160 122.576994 52.15719 72.3198 0 0
Error 178 375.3279 2.108584
Total 186 1355.9439


Drop one QTL at a time ANOVA table:
----------------------------------
df Type III SS LOD %var F value Pvalue(Chi2) Pvalue(F)
3...@35.3 2 26.68 2.789 1.968 6.327 0.002 0.00222 **
A...@6.3 2 186.72 16.397 13.771 44.277 0.000 2.22e-16 ***
3...@36.3 2 26.78 2.799 1.975 6.351 0.002 0.00217 **
3...@6.3 2 25.80 2.700 1.903 6.118 0.002 0.00269 **
---
Signif. codes: 0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

> out4<-addqtl(x, qtl=qtl3)
> summary(out4)
chr pos lod
c3.loc34 3 34.30 2.595
cA.loc1 A 5.58 0.693
2.33E+13 C 13.92 0.684

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Multiple linked QTLs
parts:
Probably the best way to deal with this is to require at least two typed markers between any two inferred QTL, or to ensure that no two inferred QTL are closer than some specified distance.

karl
